Nha Trang restaurants offer a variety of delicacies for travellers worldwide, though no trip to this coastal town is complete without sampling its star cuisine. Restaurants in Nha Trang also cater to those who fancy something from back home, as authentic French, Greek, Indian, and other international delicacies are available along Tran Phu Beach. Eating options in Nha Trang are available 24/7, with beachside seafood eateries, trendy international restaurants, vibrant street markets, and even five-star hotel dining. Unfortunate
Nov 2015 • Business
Had been looking forward in trying this place out considering the high accolades of the chef and the many positive reviews... I was looking forward to a gastronomic delight.

When we first arrived we were given a choice of where to sit which was a nice surprise. We were seated and I noticed my fork had a very large and obvious clump of dried residue of something on it. After bringing this to the waiters attention he dutifully replaced it and genuinely felt embarrassed and apologised.

After perusing the menu I decided upon the much acclaimed signature dish of the watermelon and scallop soup. This was unavailable which I thought was unusual given it was a signature dish. 

My next choice was the salmon as I remember a great review about it on this site. This too was unavailable, ok maybe I was just having rotten luck.

So now I decided on one of the duck dishes and you guessed it... This too was unavailable. So now I resorted to asking what actually was available on the menu. After the waitress went through what was available it became apparent that hardly half the dishes were only available. This in itself is not necessarily unusual in HCM but it IS unusual for a fine dining establishment such as this place.

By now I was starting to consider whether we should stay considering we came for particular dishes of which none were available... Then came the final straw... Our drinks arrived and my little miss lovely shrieked in horror as she almost gulped a bug in her drink... Now I'm not talking a flea size or ant sized bug here but a beetle sized bug.

This was finally enough for me to call the manager over and I explained all that had happened... His response: "it was out of his control".

We left, never to return again.

Great Chef = Amazing Food
Sep 2015 • Friends
Chef Jack Lee is an accomplished Vietnamese American chef who has made headlines in the U.S. and has finally brought his cooking to Vietnam. His menu offers traditional dishes, such as pizza, philly cheesesteak, and prime rib, but what makes his dishes different from the rest of Vietnam is either because of a twist on the old recipe or quality ingredients (or both). For example, instead of the traditional pizza dough, chef Jack Lee uses a puff pastry as the dough. Or the philly cheesesteak (which is a secret menu item), he uses three different cheeses (and none of them is the cheez wiz to which you may be accustomed). The prime rib is my favorite--USDA grade beef, roasted to perfection. The atmosphere is quiet and relaxing--overlooking parts of Saigon with an amphitheater next door providing free live shows. Last (but certainly not least), chef Jack Lee's radiant and lively personality makes dining there a joy--not to mention the service is on par with western standards (which is a rarity in Vietnam). It's no wonder chef Jack Lee is the next big thing in dining in Asia.

Best restaurant under Hollywood chef Jack Lee
Sep 2015 • Family
Acacia's a major surprise, hidden away on the 8th floor of the Compass Parkview building. It's one of the quieter District 1 streets, so you wouldn't expect to find Beverly Hills-style fine dining there, but in this case that's literally what you get. Acacia's cheffed by Chef Jack Lee, formerly of the Hotel Bel-Air, the guy who has cooked for pretty much every A-lister in Hollywood. What's he doing here? He's Vietnamese, and it seems for now he's moved back home.

Jack Lee cooked for our family, and it was an exceptional meal. Virtually every dish is garnished with sauces made from tropical Vietnamese fruit, and they're all original recipes. The standout for me was the fois gras, with passion fruit sauce as well as dragon fruit and kiwi. I'm usually nervous about dishes like that, but this one is incredible. For mains, I had a lamb chop with cherry sauce and mint oil, extremely fragrant with a lotus & potato mash on the side. The US Prime Rib is the dinner of champions, and we're advised by the celebrity chef to actually splash our red wine over it to enhance the flavour, which WORKS. Our kids enjoyed fun pasta dishes as a comfort food, so they were happy while we fully enjoyed our meal.
